Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

MFO (development version)

Target: v0.2.1 on CRAN. Scientific background and sources in docs/SPEC.md.

Infrastructure

  • GitHub Actions: R CMD check on macOS, Windows and Ubuntu (R devel, release, oldrel-1), test coverage with Codecov, and a pkgdown site deployed to https://jorgedelro.github.io/MFO/.
  • README rewritten for v0.2.x and generated from an executable README.Rmd.
  • Fixed the DOI of Achten et al. (2002) in DESCRIPTION.

Bug fixes

  • SIN model: MFO_kinetics() now implements equation [14] of Chenevière et al. (2009), pi^(1/s) / (pi + 2*d); v0.1.0/v0.2.0 computed pi^(1/s) / pi + 2*d. Both describe the same family of curves, so the fitted curve can be the same, but d and t take different values: the old d was not Chenevière’s dilatation and is not comparable with published values. With their Fig. 5 parameters (d = 0.18, s = 1.52, t = 0.21) the old formula put Fatmax at 28.9 %VO2max instead of 58.2 (SPEC 6.5, 19 finding 5).
  • SIN fitting procedure: MFO_kinetics() now fits the model directly to the observed steps (%MFO normalised to the highest observed step), as Chenevière et al. (2009) did. v0.1.0/v0.2.0 fitted a grid of ≥ 50 points predicted by a third-degree polynomial, which inflated n and shrank the standard errors of d, s and t. FatMax_SIN and Fatmin now come from closed forms derived from eq. [14], and Fatmin is the second zero of the curve, (π + d − t)/K, instead of the first grid point below 5 % of MFO. Example data (Frayn): d 0.144 -> −0.385, s 0.935 -> 0.910, t −0.093 -> 0.355, FatMax_SIN 36.0 -> 36.2, Fatmin 76.0 -> 76.4 %VO2max, R² 0.997 -> 0.965 (now on the observed steps); standard errors grow 20–60 fold to their honest size. With negative_FAT = "exclude" or RER_cutoff = 1 (Chenevière’s step selection) the example gives s = 0.54 and Fatmin = 85.3 %VO2max: the SIN is sensitive to the last step, see ?MFO_kinetics (SPEC 6.5, 19 findings 3 and 7).
  • MFO_kinetics() now distinguishes two warnings: with fewer than 4 steps the SIN cannot be fitted (convergence = FALSE, as before); with 4 or 5 steps it is fitted but warns that the fit is unreliable and that at least 6 steps are recommended (SPEC 6.5).
  • VO2max from db_graded is now the highest rolling mean over the new vo2max_window argument (default 30 s) instead of the single highest record. If the window is not a multiple of step_time, the number of records is rounded up (30 s with 20-s records = 2 records = 40 s) and a message reports the effective window. Fatmax, the Fatmax zone and the crossover point (%VO2max) increase by the ratio old/new VO2max; MFO (g/min) is unchanged. In the example data VO2max drops from 3442 to 3315 ml/min and Fatmax moves from 34.8 to 36.2 %VO2max. Use vo2max_window = step_time to reproduce v0.2.0 (SPEC 9.5, 14).
  • Resting substrate oxidation (x_CHO, x_FAT, x_Kcal) now uses the same author equations as the test; it always used Frayn before. Jeukendrup & Wallis (2005) propose no resting equation: with author = "Jeukendrup" the package uses the 100 % glucose pair derived from their Table 4 constants (CHO = 4.58519 VCO2 − 3.22597 VO2, FAT = 1.69469 VO2 − 1.70130 VCO2), documented as a package decision. MFO and Fatmax are not affected because the resting row is not part of the fit. Example data with "Peronnet": resting CHO 0.130 -> 0.134 g/min, FAT 0.0726 -> 0.0723 g/min (SPEC 9.5).
  • With author = "Jeukendrup", MFO() now warns once when exercise steps fall outside 40–75 %VO2max, the range of the Jeukendrup & Wallis (2005, Table 5) equations, and lists their intensities; those steps were extrapolated silently before. Steps removed by RER_cutoff and the resting row never warn. Values are unchanged (SPEC 3, 9.5).
  • substrate_oxidation() no longer fails on vectors with author = "Jeukendrup"; each value picks its own equation.
  • When both VO2max and db_graded are given, VO2max is now used and db_graded is ignored with a warning (v0.2.0 silently used db_graded).

Coefficient policy

  • Coefficients printed in the source are used as printed and cited by table or equation; derived coefficients are used only where the source prints no equation, with the derivation explained in the documentation (SPEC 19). Exercise equations of Jeukendrup & Wallis (2005, Table 5) and Frayn (1983) are used as printed; their derivation from the published O2/CO2 constants is kept as a cross-check test.

New features

  • MFO_kinetics() and MFOs() gain fatmin_threshold (default NULL, Fatmin at the second zero of the SIN curve); a proportion of MFO such as 0.05 gives the intensity above Fatmax where fat oxidation falls to that fraction, in closed form. The kinetics plot now shows the observed steps and draws the fitted curve between its two zeros (SPEC 19, finding 3).
  • MFO() and MFOs() gain include_basal (default FALSE). With TRUE the resting row enters MFO_db as step 0 and is part of the P3/P2 fit, as in Montes de Oca et al. (2021). The default reproduces v0.1.0/v0.2.0, which silently lost the resting row because its HR is NA; the exclusion is now explicit and no longer depends on missing HR. Example data, Frayn, P3: MFO 0.3167 -> 0.3225 g/min and Fatmax 36.17 -> 36.11 %VO2max with TRUE (SPEC 9.5).
  • MFO() returns VO2max, VO2max_window (effective, s) and VO2max_window_requested; MFOs() gains vo2max_window and the columns VO2max and VO2max_window.

Known issues (scheduled for this release)

Found while verifying the code against the primary sources (SPEC sections 9.5 and 19):

  • method = "MRER" is a measured-values method on 1.7 * (1 - RER) * VO2, not the two-regression MRER procedure.
  • MFO_db$Load is a synthetic step index, not measured load.
  • Péronnet & Massicotte (1991) print no equations: the package uses rounded constants instead of the coefficients derived from their Table 1 (4.58519/3.22597; 1.69469/1.70130); energy equivalents are 4/9 kcal/g for all equations (Jeukendrup & Wallis 2005, Table 5, give CHO 3.95 kcal/g at 40–50 %VO2max, 4.07 kcal/g at 50–75 % and fat 9.75 kcal/g).

MFO 0.2.0

GitHub release (February 2026). Not submitted to CRAN.

New features

  • MFO() gains method to choose the curve-fitting method: "P3" (third-degree polynomial, new default), "P2" and "MRER". Version 0.1.0 always used a second-degree polynomial.
  • MFO() gains author = "Peronnet" (Péronnet & Massicotte, 1991) in addition to "Frayn" and "Jeukendrup".
  • New protocol arguments in MFO() and MFOs(): step_duration (default 180 s) and steady_state_duration (default 60 s).
  • New artefact handling: RER_cutoff removes steps above an RER threshold; negative_FAT chooses whether negative fat oxidation is truncated to 0, excluded or kept.
  • New outputs in MFO(): Fatmax zone (fat oxidation within 10 % of MFO), crossover point, heart rate at Fatmax and Fatmax as %HRmax (HRmax), MFO relative to body mass (body_mass) and to fat-free mass (fat_free_mass), and R_squared / RMSE of the fit.
  • MFO_kinetics() now returns standard errors of d, s and t, FatMax_SIN, Fatmin, R_squared, RMSE and a convergence flag, and handles fitting failures without stopping.
  • MFOs() passes all new MFO() arguments through and gains output_format ("xlsx", "csv" or "rds").
  • Internal helper to average breath-by-breath data into fixed intervals.

Other changes

  • Requires R >= 4.1.0 (was R >= 2.10).
  • Expanded unit tests.

MFO 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2022-02-11

First CRAN release (February 2022).

  • MFO() computes MFO and Fatmax from resting, incremental and maximal test data, with Frayn (1983) or Jeukendrup & Wallis (2005) equations and a second-degree polynomial fit.
  • MFO_kinetics() fits the SIN model of Cheneviere et al. (2009) and returns dilatation, symmetry and translation.
  • MFOs() processes a folder of participants.
